title: Pairs and odd ones out
_map: Pairs and odd ones out (Y2). Big idea: even numbers split into pairs; odd numbers always leave one over. Is odd + odd odd or even? Test it and make a rule.
_story: Steve's sheep go on a walk in pairs, holding hooves. Some walks leave one sheep sad and alone. He tests numbers like a scientist, names even and odd, then runs an experiment: what happens when two odd groups meet?
_stepChain: counting → pairs → some numbers make only pairs → some leave one over → even → odd → predict odd + odd → test with sheep → rule

talk.ask: What's the difference between an even number and an odd number?
talk.goodAnswer: even numbers make pairs with none left over; odd numbers always have one left over.

talk.ask: Why is odd + odd always even?
talk.goodAnswer: each odd group has one left over, and the two left-over ones pair up with each other.

handsOn: Grab a handful of Lego bricks and pair them up. Odd or even? Grab another handful, put both together, and check again. Can you find an odd + odd that isn't even?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: My sheep love going for walks, two by two, side by side. But sometimes one sheep has nobody to walk with, and it looks so sad!
Be a scientist. Choose how many sheep go for a walk, then tap the hammer. Does everyone get a partner? Try lots of numbers.
Some numbers make pairs with nobody left out: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Numbers like those are called even.
Other numbers always leave one sheep on its own: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Numbers like those are called odd.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Experiment time! 3 sheep meet 5 sheep. 3 is odd, and 5 is odd. I think two odd groups must make an even bigger odd group!

question.prompt: What do you think? Will they be odd or even together?
question.reveal: Even! 3 and 5 make 8. Each odd group had one sheep on its own, and those two lonely sheep became a new pair.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Was that a lucky accident? Let's test again. 7 sheep meet 9 sheep.

question.onRight: Yes. You used the rule: the two lonely sheep make a pair, so it's even again.

0.mistake: hasn't yet connected the two left-over sheep pairing up
0.hint: 7 has one sheep left over. 9 has one sheep left over. What can those two do?
0.say: 7 has one sheep without a partner, and so does 9. Those two walk together as a new pair. 7 and 9 make 16, and 16 is even.

question.reveal: 16 sheep: all in pairs. Odd and odd always make even.

rule.text: Even makes pairs. Odd has one left over.
rule.ask: Can you say what makes a number odd, and what odd plus odd makes? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Even numbers make pairs with none left over. Odd numbers always have one left over. And odd plus odd is always even.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: is odd + even odd or even? Guess, then test it with Lego.
bonus.reveal: Odd. The even group is all pairs, and the odd group still has its one left over.
